App.Title: Warcraft II Remastered — Quality of Life Mods
Colors.Intro: Units on the battlefield, minimap, victory and ally screen all follow the selected colors.
ColorBlind.DefaultHint: Pick a preset to load suggested player colors for that type of color blindness. Press Apply to use them in-game.
ColorBlind.CustomHint: Custom player colors. Edit each slot (or use the pickers), then press Apply to use them in-game.
ColorBlind.Deuteranopia.Hint: Green-blind (most common): suggested colors avoid red/green pairs and lean on blue, orange, yellow, and magenta.
ColorBlind.Protanopia.Hint: Red-blind: suggested colors emphasize blue, yellow, and cyan so red and green no longer look alike.
ColorBlind.Tritanopia.Hint: Blue-yellow blind: suggested colors avoid blue/yellow confusion and use red, orange, teal, and purple instead.
Feature.Intro: Optional feature mods for multiplayer games. Each mod is compatible with the others — you can use them individually or simultaneously.
Feature.MarkGoneHumans.Help: When a human player leaves, disconnects, or is eliminated, their name turns red on the alliances screen. Works on its own or together with Mark gone computers.
Feature.MarkGoneComputers.Help: When a computer opponent is wiped out or eliminated, its name turns red on the alliances screen. Works in games that also have human players — only computer slots are marked.
Feature.AnnounceComputers.Help: Gives textual feedback when a computer player has been wiped out.
Feature.ChatColoredNames: Show chat names in player color
Feature.ChatColoredNames.Help: Multiplayer chat lines from a player use that player's current color from Player colors. The message text remains white and clearly visible. Leave and drop messages also show the leaving player's name in their color.
Feature.ChatTimestamps.Help: Every chat line starts with the clock time it appeared, like [21:08].
Feature.LobbyTeamNumber.Help: Puts the multiplayer team number in front of each player's name on the alliances screen, making it easier to observe games without confusion.
Feature.LobbyMapClickOpen.Help: In a multiplayer lobby, click the map name to open its preview image. Make sure to download the map images manually or by using this application under the Maps tab. Previews are read from your configured map images folder (Paths).
Feature.UpgradeNotifications.Help: Gold chat notifications when a building upgrade completes. Temporarily unavailable while this feature is being reworked.
Feature.ObserveAfterEnd.Help: Temporarily unavailable while this feature is being reworked.
Bugfixes.ChatDuringPause.Help: Lets you read, type, and send chat while the multiplayer game is paused. Both players need this bug fix installed — if only one side has it, that player can send, but the other only sees the message after unpause if the chat is within its timeframe.
Bugfixes.ChatHistory.Help: Press Page Up, or hold Ctrl and press Arrow Up, in a match to bring back earlier chat messages, page by page. Page Down, or Ctrl+Arrow Down, moves forward again and returns to live chat. The last 64 messages of the current game are kept — every new game starts fresh.
Bugfixes.MpLobbyChatScroll.Help: Keeps multiplayer lobby chat scroll position when a player changes race (random, orc, or human). Vanilla resets the chat to the top on every slot refresh.
Bugfixes.CastleGoldTooltip.Help: Upgrading a Keep to a Castle (Humans) or a Stronghold to a Fortress (Orcs) grants +20% gold production, but the build tooltip incorrectly says +25%.
Network.Intro: Lockstep tick-gap monitor for MP debug (v1). Not real per-player ping — a log foundation for a future /jitter command.
Network.Monitor.Help: V1 debug tool: during an MP match this measures time between game ticks (lockstep — everyone shares the same tick). Large gaps mean hitch/stall, not ICMP ping per player. Human players only in the list (no Computer). Writes a snapshot every second to %TEMP%\war2_network_monitor.log for later /jitter and analysis.
Settings.Language.Help: Choose the language for this app. Your choice is saved automatically.
Settings.ColorBlindMode.Help: Makes this app easier to read: light background, clear borders, and high-contrast text. Does not change in-game colors.
Settings.RestoreClean.Help: Restore (fast) puts back the vanilla files from this app's local backup and turns extras off. Battle.net Scan and Repair is slower and the fallback if you prefer Blizzard's repair.
About.Intro: About this Quality of Life Mods tool.
About.AppTitle: Warcraft II Remastered — Quality of Life Mods
About.Body: Work in progress. I welcome hints, tips, and suggestions — please share what would help you. Author: Avent (Battle.net account).
About.HowItWorks.Body: 1. Change colors, features, or bug fixes. 2. Press Apply (local vanilla backup). 3. Restart Warcraft II Remastered. 4. Use Settings to restore if needed. Hooks keep working after you close this app via a small Windows watcher.
Paths.Intro: Set your Warcraft II Remastered paths. Changes are saved automatically.
Paths.GameInstall.Help: Choose the folder that contains Warcraft II Remastered (the one with an x86 folder). Mods and bug fixes install here. If the initial path is accepted, no changes are needed.
Paths.MapEditor.Help: Points to Warcraft II Map Editor.exe inside your install. Open launches the map editor. Useful for quick access.
Paths.MapsFolder.Help: The folder where your custom maps live (usually x86\Maps). Download saves .pud maps from warcraft2.site into the downloads subfolder. Open shows the folder in Explorer.
